method.scope: the human correction and retest loop only: POST /api/v1/machine/answers, POST /api/v1/machine/corrections, POST /api/v1/machine/retests, the machine task receipts they read/write, and the review path that promotes a correction
method.line_number_pin: The G4 machine-loop code is committed at worktree HEAD ed47205c8c320072212c14c58d8258239b028fdb. Line numbers in code_location are HEAD line numbers. Reason: while this audit ran, the working tree was being edited concurrently and uncommitted (git status shows runtime/mod.rs, archeaxis-archive/src/lib.rs, archeaxis-domain/src/vault.rs, archeaxis-store-sqlite/src/lib.rs dirty). git diff shows those edits are NEW G2 vault-link routes/functions only; the record_correction / run_retest / machine_answer code is byte-identical at HEAD and in the working tree, but the inserted vault_links_record function shifts the working-tree line numbers of run_retest (HEAD 316, working tree 401) and machine_answer (HEAD 494, working tree 579). Every citation therefore also carries the quoted source text so it stays locatable if the file moves again.
notes: attempts.rs was inspected as the task named it as 'the route table', but it is the job-kind to extraction-capability table (attempts.rs:31-79). It contains no machine route and no correction/retest entry; the HTTP registrations are runtime/mod.rs:29-67 and lib.rs:90-91. Any claim sited against attempts.rs for this loop would have no code location and is reported as such.
No existing file was modified. The only write of this audit is this JSON file.

Unverifiable-by-static-read items are named as such in the relevant note rather than silently accepted: worker/model behavior and live HTTP statuses were read from source and from the repository's own contract tests, not re-observed on a running Core.

The HTTP handler does NOT check failure itself; it only checks existence (runtime/mod.rs:341-359).

claims.claim: "a real Machine Task driving a model" is listed as not yet real

What is genuinely missing is the baseline: no Core route can produce a machine task receipt whose outcome is `failed` from a model run (/machine/answers writes nothing and /machine/retests hard-codes outcome "succeeded" at 454), so the failed task a retest must point at has to be declared by a machine client through /machine/tasks. The item should say that, not that no task drives a model.

The defensible remaining gap is narrower and should be stated instead: the binding is to a caller-supplied answer string, not to a recorded machine answer (CorrectionBody 636-651 holds no task or answer id).

claims.claim: "correction-bound retest" is listed as not yet real
claims.code_location: crates/archeaxis-api/src/runtime/mod.rs:316-487 (run_retest: retest_of must name a failed task, knowledge_id supplies the context at 435-447 and becomes the receipt's knowledge_version at 433); RetestBody at 671-685 has no correction id or candidate id field
claims.note: A correction-bound retest is runnable: the caller names the corrected item as knowledge_id and the failed task as retest_of, which is what the repository's own probe effectively does with a successor revision. What is not enforced is the binding: nothing checks that knowledge_id is the correction, the correction candidate, or even different from the item the failed task used, and there is no correction id in the body. State the weak binding rather than calling the capability absent.

most_serious_discrepancy.finding: The HTTP contract tells a client that the G4 machine routes do not exist, while the same document documents them and the code registers them. AAOS-PRODUCTION-HTTP-CONTRACT-20261001.md:526-528 says the machine loop's blocker is wiring and that "no route reaches the model yet"; lines 580-584 say "What does not exist is a Core route that drives it" and that "the missing piece is a Core route that accepts a question", instructing the UI to show machine answering as not connected. The routes are registered at crates/archeaxis-api/src/runtime/mod.rs:48, 55 and 58, the answer handler accepts `question` (MachineAnswerBody, runtime/mod.rs:610-619) and drives the worker through crates/archeaxis-application/src/executor.rs:133-199, and the same document's own section 3 (lines 200-203) describes all three routes as part of the production inventory.
most_serious_discrepancy.why_most_serious: It is the only finding that is both contradicted by the code and self-contradictory inside the document that is the declared hand-off surface for the UI, and its practical effect is the opposite of a harmless overstatement: a client that follows section 6/8 will not call the routes G4 was built to deliver, so a documented capability stays invisible.
most_serious_discrepancy.runner_up: The second most serious is the accepted-knowledge guarantee in the machine answer path: the document says /machine/answers asks about "one accepted knowledge item" (line 203) and the G4 definition of done says "a real model answers from accepted knowledge over HTTP" (AAOS-EXECUTION-ORDER-AND-DOD-20261002.json:119), but the context query at crates/archeaxis-api/src/runtime/mod.rs:516-517 has no status predicate, so a rejected, deprecated or superseded body can ground a machine answer. This is a governance claim the Core does not enforce (crates/archeaxis-domain/src/knowledge.rs:443-461 defines active knowledge and is never consulted on this path).

answers_to_the_six_questions.1_retest_requires_failed: Yes, in the domain, not in the handler. Exact guard: crates/archeaxis-domain/src/machine.rs:151 `if outcome.as_deref() != Some("failed") {` with the message at 152-154. The handler only checks existence (runtime/mod.rs:341-359), so the refusal surfaces as 500 after the model has already run (runtime/mod.rs:461-465).
answers_to_the_six_questions.2_core_decides_whether_the_correction_he: No document claims it, and the code does not do it. runtime/mod.rs:313-315 and 482-484 state the opposite; the response (467-486) has no verdict field.
answers_to_the_six_questions.3_correction_status: Stored as a candidate, not accepted knowledge. Exactly: knowledge_type OBSERVATION, status "candidate", evidence_status "UNSOURCED", created_by "human", no anchor (runtime/mod.rs:187-199); no knowledge_v3_metadata row is created (knowledge.rs:122).
answers_to_the_six_questions.4_machine_can_record_or_accept_a_correct: Neither. Record is refused at runtime/mod.rs:146-147 (403, "a correction is a human act; a machine principal cannot record one"); accept is refused at lib.rs:1573-1581 (403, "machine principal cannot perform human review actions").
answers_to_the_six_questions.5_retest_receipt_when_the_model_fails: Nothing at all is recorded. runtime/mod.rs:403-408 returns 503 from the model error before the only write (437-460).
answers_to_the_six_questions.6_retest_of_locations: Both. Column machine_tasks.retest_of (machine.rs:35), written at machine.rs:171/184 from runtime/mod.rs:456, read back at machine.rs:217-218/231, and present in the response at runtime/mod.rs:470.

cross_cutting_observations: The two 2026-10-01/2026-10-02 documents disagree about whether the G4 routes exist. AAOS-EXECUTION-ORDER-AND-DOD-20261002.json:122-126 and 141-147 record them as delivered; AAOS-PRODUCTION-HTTP-CONTRACT-20261001.md:526-528 and 580-584 record them as absent; AAOS-FAST-CLOSURE-GOLDEN-PATH-V1-20261002.json:45-52 records the machine half as unwired. The code (worktree HEAD ed47205c) is on the side of the execution-order document.

The loop's links are weaker than the prose implies in three places, all because identity is asserted by the caller rather than checked by the Core: the correction's `machine_answer` is free text with no answer id (runtime/mod.rs:643, 206-208); the retest's `question` need not match the original, which is not stored (runtime/mod.rs:395 vs machine.rs:24-37); and the retest's `knowledge_id` need not be the correction (runtime/mod.rs:433, 435-447). Each of the three documents describes the link as if it were verified.

The baseline failure a retest must point at cannot be produced by any Core route that calls the model: /machine/answers records nothing (runtime/mod.rs:494-568), /machine/retests hard-codes outcome "succeeded" (runtime/mod.rs:454), and /machine/tasks accepts the outcome from a machine client (lib.rs:406, machine-only at 389). The documents describe the loop as if the failure were observed; in code it is declared.

No document claim about this loop was found to be unverifiable from source. Two are verifiable only in the negative sense and are marked in their notes: the worker's own live behaviour (line 535 evidence row, contract tests, executor.rs) and whether a real human ever performs the correction step (AAOS-EXECUTION-ORDER-AND-DOD-20261002.json:134-137 correctly lists that as needing a person, which is an open item rather than a false claim).

attempts.rs, which the audit brief named as the route table, holds no machine, correction or retest entry (attempts.rs:31-79 is the job-kind to extraction-capability map). Claims about this loop must be sited against runtime/mod.rs:29-67 and lib.rs:90-91 instead; where a claim was checked against attempts.rs it would have had no code location.

The audited G4 code is committed at HEAD ed47205c; the working tree was dirty with unrelated G2 vault-link edits during this audit (runtime/mod.rs hash changed twice while reading), which is why every code_location carries quoted source text as well as a HEAD line number.
